newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P cuts JAL rating outlook to negative.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts JAL rating outlook to negative.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Tuesday that it had revised its rating outlook for Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) to negative from stable while affirming its BBB+ long-term rating for the airline.
S&P said in a statement that it had also affirmed its A-2 commercial paper rating of JAL Capital Corp.

"JAL needs to bolster its profitability and cash flow and reduce its financial risk ahead of further deregulation and capacity increases. Failure to move further in this direction could lead to a downgrade," S&P said.
S&P said JAL's financial profile was weak for the rating category.
On the consolidated basis, its total debt to capital was more than 80 percent, the highest among investment-grade international peers, S&P said.
While JAL's earnings and cash flow had improved from their lows in 1992/93, S&P said it expected them to have weakened again in 1996/97 following recent fuel-price increases.

It said it expected any improvement in the airline's financial profile to be limited, as it would likely need to make additional investments in aircraft to take advantage of capacity expansions at Haneda and Narita airports over the next few years.
